# Polyworld fast-XP

Run game matches synchronously and download replays and your uploaded bots' logs.
Connect to the Softmax Tailscale network. Send Content-Type: application/json;
the hosted service needs no caller token or Authorization header.

## Choose a game

| Game | POST endpoint | Seats | BASIC source limit | Default max_ticks | Default execution deadline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gota | /v1/games/gota/run | 10 | 64 KiB | 28800 | 120 seconds |
| Paintbot | /v1/games/paintbot-pw/run | 16 | 128 KiB | 14400 | 300 seconds |
| Archers Warriors Mages | /v1/games/awm/run | 5 | 256 KiB | 28800 | 120 seconds |

GET /v1/metrics lists this server's installed games in games. A run endpoint
for a game that is not installed returns 404. All installed games share one
worker pool and queue. Matches run at full compute speed; external LLM/oracle
calls are unavailable. AWM uses the league's five-player Competition variant.

Game references:
- [Gota run guide](/docs/gota/run.md)
- [Paintbot run guide](/docs/paintbot-pw/run.md)
- [Archers Warriors Mages run guide](/docs/awm/run.md)

## Make a request

Send the following JSON to your chosen game's POST endpoint:

```json
{
  "seed": 2026,
  "roster": [
    {"slot": 0, "player": {"source": "end\n"}},
    {"player": {"policy_ref": "opponent-name:v12"}}
  ],
  "num_episodes": 1,
  "config": {"max_ticks": 240}
}
```

Replace end with your complete BASIC script and opponent-name:v12 with a real
submitted policy. The example bot passes its turns; it is not competitive.
For a first run without an opponent reference, use:
{"seed":2026,"roster":[{"player":{"source":"end\n"}}],"config":{"max_ticks":240}}
This fills every seat with your uploaded script.

Each player contains exactly one of:
- source: nonempty BASIC source text, within the game's source limit above.
- package_base64: a standard padded base64 ZIP in that game's production policy
  format, with no whitespace. Gota and AWM accept ZIPs up to 16 MiB; Paintbot
  accepts up to 16920576 bytes. Base64 encoding is additional.
- policy_ref: an exact submitted policy label such as my-bot:v12, or a
  policy-version UUID. The server fetches opponents using its own Observatory
  credential; callers do not need opponents' source or download permissions.

Supply between one and the game's seat count roster entries. Optional slot
pins an entry to that zero-based seat; -1 (the default) fills open seats
cyclically in roster order. Duplicate pinned slots are invalid. At least one
unpinned entry is required unless every seat is pinned. Pinned entries do not
also fill open seats. Paintbot's even seats are red and odd seats are blue.

seed is a required signed 32-bit integer. num_episodes is optional, 1–10,
default 1: each game increments the seed and rotates unpinned entries, while
pinned seats stay fixed. The final seed must fit in the signed 32-bit range.
config.max_ticks is optional, 1–28800, with the game defaults above. AWM ticks
are game actions; Gota and Paintbot ticks are simulation steps. Other game
configuration is fixed to the league defaults. Unknown fields are rejected.
JSON bodies are limited to 224 MiB, or 352 MiB when Paintbot is installed.

## Read the response

A successful response is application/zip. One game contains replay.replay and
logs/slot-N.txt for seats populated from source or package_base64. Only uploaded
seats' logs are returned. Policy-reference logs and source remain private,
even if the caller owns that submitted policy. No response includes bot source,
model files, credentials or artifact download URLs.

A batch contains manifest.json and games/000/, games/001/, etc. Each manifest
record includes status, seed, seating as roster-entry indexes, active_bots,
artifact paths and queue/worker timings. HTTP 200 batches may contain failed
games: inspect each game's http_status before using its replay. Successful
games remain available when another game fails. A failed single game returns
an HTTP error with JSON {"error":"message"}.

Save the response. There is no polling or stored-results endpoint. Games queue
when workers are busy; allow a long client timeout for batches and queueing.
Accepted work finishes if the caller disconnects, then artifacts are discarded.
X-Request-ID correlates with server logs. Server-Timing reports fetch, queue,
worker, ZIP and total server milliseconds; gameplay is included only when the
game supplies it. Worker includes process startup, staging and artifact writing,
so it is not pure simulation time. Queue/worker/gameplay sum across batch games;
run measures batch wall time. Timings exclude client upload/download.

Errors use JSON {"error":"message"}: 400 invalid input or ambiguous policy,
404 unknown route or policy, 409 no downloadable policy file, 413 oversized
input, 415 wrong content type, 422 policy loading or compilation failure,
500 worker failure, 502 policy lookup/download/integrity failure, 503 shutdown
or missing server credential, and 504 fetch or execution timeout. Only uploaded
bot diagnostics are disclosed. 429 means all 16 request admissions are used;
honor Retry-After before retrying. There are no automatic retries.

GET / shows the performance dashboard. GET /healthz returns ok.
GET /v1/metrics?minutes=60 returns dashboard data; windows are 15, 60 or 1440.
History stays in memory for 24 hours and resets on restart.
